consumers.evidence: The confirmed tray, browser console, phone PWA, five-area information architecture, and Redline boundaries remain authoritative.
DESKTOP-TRAY-WEB-CONSOLE-001 remains user_confirmed with deferred automatic download, WebView2, and full native UI scope.
The command-only current runtime is explicitly classified as the transitional predecessor; the contract replaces port-only health with proven ownership and identity.
All web, service, lifecycle, packaging, device, connection, version, and verification consumers are within the authorized implementation scope.
The end-to-end chain is launcher to single tray Owner to identified Node service to browser console, with phone PWA and persistent device data kept separate.

The current hidden Node launcher, port-based stop logic, loopback APIs, durable SessionStore, setup screen, LAN discovery, and packaging mechanisms were inspected and bound to their implementation deltas.
The implementation uses Windows PowerShell STA and WinForms already present on target Windows plus the bundled Node runtime; Electron, WebView2, online update, and new external runtimes are excluded.
Tray and service ownership, runtime/tray receipts, process proof, graceful replacement order, fail-closed unknown-process behavior, and unchanged trusted-device ownership are frozen.

Version/build identity comes from packaged project metadata, runtime records live in LOCALAPPDATA, installation configuration remains in .env, and Redline token values are copied into project-owned CSS without runtime cross-repo dependency.

Automated identity, device, routing, style-scope, build and package checks plus real tray, replacement, unknown-port, browser, responsive, phone-regression, and data-retention acceptance are explicit.
The next authorized work is the complete tray and Redline browser-console delivery; automatic download, WebView2, full native UI, public internet, and release remain deferred.
Implementation is authorized on branch codex/desktop-tray-redline in E:/work/project/codexPWA using Cursor CLI, without a Task Control shell or external release actions.
